turns.en: I need to take a little blood from you now. Sharp scratch coming... well done, all finished. Just press on that for me.
turns.cy: Dw i angen cymryd chydig o waed gynnoch chi rŵan. Crafiad siarp yn dod... da iawn chi, wedi gorffen. Pwyswch ar hwnna i mi.
chunks: I need to take a little blood from you now
Dw i angen cymryd chydig o waed gynnoch chi rŵan
the bare angen need-frame (R3); Welsh takes blood 'with' the person — the conjugated gan, not 'from'
English's bare progressive has no copula to render; Welsh leaves the yn-participle standing
Just press on that for me

turns.en: Go on then. I'm used to it by now.
turns.cy: Ewch amdani 'ta. Dw i wedi arfer erbyn hyn.
chunks: I'm used to it by now
Dw i wedi arfer erbyn hyn
English's 'to it' complement erases — arfer stands alone

turns.en: There we are - in first time. Keep pressing for a minute. You might get a little bruise, nothing to worry about.
turns.cy: Dyna ni — i mewn y tro cynta. Daliwch i bwyso am funud. Ella cewch chi glais bach, dim byd i boeni amdano fo.
chunks: 'keep -ing' → dal i + verbal noun, the same frame as 'we keep checking'
You might get a little bruise
the modal relocation: adverb ella + a plain future
dim byd i boeni amdano fo

turns.en: First time! You're hired. Usually I'm like a pin cushion.
turns.cy: Y tro cynta! Dach chi wedi'ch cyflogi. Fel arfer dw i fel pincas.
chunks: the wedi-passive (§4), which is how Welsh does English's be-passive
Usually I'm like a pin cushion
Fel arfer dw i fel pincas
pincas is the Welsh word, not a borrowing

turns.en: I'll take the compliment. That's you done - the doctor will have the results tomorrow.
turns.cy: Mi gymra i'r ganmoliaeth. Dyna chi wedi gorffen — mi fydd y canlyniadau gan y doctor fory.
chunks: canmoliaeth is feminine, so the article mutates it
the doctor will have the results tomorrow
mi fydd y canlyniadau gan y doctor fory
possession relocates to gan, and the two arguments swap places

turns.en: Is that it? You're a wonder.
turns.cy: Ai dyna'r cwbl? Dach chi'n rhyfeddod.
chunks: the identificatory question particle ai, which English has no word for

turns.en: I need to take a little blood now. Sharp scratch coming...
turns.cy: Dw i angen cymryd chydig o waed rŵan. Crafiad siarp yn dod...
chunks: I need to take a little blood now
Dw i angen cymryd chydig o waed rŵan
distinct from 'a little blood FROM YOU' → …gynnoch chi

turns.en: How much are you taking? What's this one for?
turns.cy: Faint dach chi'n ei gymryd? I be mae'r un yma?
chunks: the resumptive ei, obligatory after a fronted interrogative
the purpose-cleft as a question, one form course-wide (R3)

turns.en: Just two little bottles. The doctor's checking your kidneys and your blood count - seeing how you're doing on the new tablets.
turns.cy: Dim ond dwy botel fach. Mae'r doctor yn tsiecio'ch arennau chi a'ch cyfrif gwaed chi — gweld sut dach chi'n gneud ar y tabledi newydd.
chunks: restrictive 'just' → dim ond; potel feminine, so dwy + soft mutation
The doctor's checking your kidneys and your blood count
Mae'r doctor yn tsiecio'ch arennau chi a'ch cyfrif gwaed chi
seeing how you're doing on the new tablets
gweld sut dach chi'n gneud ar y tabledi newydd

turns.en: Kidneys? Nobody said anything about my kidneys. Are they alright?
turns.cy: Arennau? Ddeudodd neb ddim byd am fy arennau i. Ydyn nhw'n iawn?
chunks: Nobody said anything about my kidneys
Ddeudodd neb ddim byd am fy arennau i
Welsh negative concord: neb and dim byd stack where English allows only one negative

turns.en: Nothing's wrong - it's routine. The tablets can be hard on kidneys, so we keep an eye. All finished, look - press on that for me.
turns.cy: Does 'na ddim byd o'i le — trefn arferol ydy o. Mi fedar y tabledi fod yn galed ar yr arennau, felly dan ni'n cadw golwg. Wedi gorffen, ylwch — pwyswch ar hwnna i mi.
chunks: English's negative subject relocates to a negative existential
The tablets can be hard on kidneys
Mi fedar y tabledi fod yn galed ar yr arennau
English's 'an eye' erases into the fixed cadw golwg

turns.en: A bruise won't kill me. Thank you, love.
turns.cy: Wneith clais ddim fy lladd i. Diolch, del.
chunks: Wneith clais ddim fy lladd i
the English indefinite article erases; the periphrastic future negates around the object

turns.en: I need to take a little blood from you. Sharp scratch coming now.
turns.cy: Dw i angen cymryd chydig o waed gynnoch chi. Crafiad siarp yn dod rŵan.
chunks: I need to take a little blood from you
Dw i angen cymryd chydig o waed gynnoch chi

turns.en: I'm terrible with needles. Can I look away? Talk to me about something else.
turns.cy: Dw i'n ofnadwy efo nodwyddau. Ga i edrych i ffwrdd? Siaradwch efo fi am rywbeth arall.
chunks: one form for 'I'm terrible with X', as at 'terrible with names'
Talk to me about something else
Siaradwch efo fi am rywbeth arall

turns.en: Look away, that's fine - lots of people do. Tell me about your grandchildren, and it'll be done before you know it.
turns.cy: Edrychwch i ffwrdd, mae hynny'n iawn — mae 'na lot o bobl yn gneud. Deudwch wrtha i am eich wyrion, ac mi fydd o wedi'i neud cyn i chi sylwi.
chunks: Edrychwch i ffwrdd, mae hynny'n iawn
mae 'na lot o bobl yn gneud
English's dummy 'do' has no Welsh reflex — the full verb must be restated
Deudwch wrtha i am eich wyrion
and it'll be done before you know it
ac mi fydd o wedi'i neud cyn i chi sylwi
the wedi-passive; and 'before you know it' becomes 'before you notice', dodging the gwybod/nabod fork (S5)

turns.en: Well, there's four of them, so that'll take us a while...
turns.cy: Wel, mae 'na bedwar ohonyn nhw, felly mi gymrith hynny sbel i ni...
chunks: so that'll take us a while...
felly mi gymrith hynny sbel i ni...
English's ditransitive 'take us a while' relocates: the beneficiary becomes a prepositional i ni

turns.en: Four! Start with the eldest - there, all done already. See?
turns.cy: Pedwar! Dechreuwch efo'r hyna — dyna ni, wedi gorffen yn barod. Ylwch?
chunks: dyna ni, wedi gorffen yn barod

turns.en: Is that it? You distracted me a treat.
turns.cy: Ai dyna'r cwbl? Mi wnaethoch chi dynnu fy sylw i'n champion.
chunks: Mi wnaethoch chi dynnu fy sylw i'n champion
English's 'distract' becomes 'pull my attention', and the 'a treat' adverbial lands on champion, the corpus's own register word
